passage.text: If you walk around the old town in Bangkok, you might see huge, colorful paintings on the walls of old buildings.
passage.reading: ɪf juː ˈwɔːk əˈraʊnd ði ˈoʊld ˈtaʊn ɪn ˈbæŋkɑːk, juː maɪt ˈsiː ˈhjuːdʒ, ˈkʌlərfəl ˈpeɪntɪŋz ɑːn ðə ˈwɔːlz əv ˈoʊld ˈbɪldɪŋz.

passage.text: Many of them were painted by Mook, a twenty-six-year-old street artist.
passage.reading: ˈmɛni əv ðɛm wɜːr ˈpeɪntɪd baɪ ˈmuːk, ə ˌtwɛnti ˌsɪks ˌjɪr ˌoʊld ˈstriːt ˌɑːrtɪst.

passage.text: Mook grew up in a small village in northeastern Thailand.
passage.reading: ˈmuːk ˈɡruː ˈʌp ɪn ə ˈsmɔːl ˈvɪlɪdʒ ɪn ˌnɔːrθˈiːstərn ˈtaɪlænd.

passage.text: She was always artistic, and she spent hours drawing the rice fields.
passage.reading: ʃiː wʌz ˈɔːlweɪz ɑːrˈtɪstɪk, ənd ʃiː ˈspɛnt ˈaʊərz ˈdrɔːɪŋ ðə ˈraɪs ˌfiːldz.

passage.text: When she moved to Bangkok to study art, she discovered graffiti.
passage.reading: wɛn ʃiː ˈmuːvd tə ˈbæŋkɑːk tə ˈstʌdi ˈɑːrt, ʃiː dɪˈskʌvərd ɡrəˈfiːti.

passage.text: "At first, I painted at night, because it was illegal," she says.
passage.reading: ət ˈfɜːrst, aɪ ˈpeɪntɪd ət ˈnaɪt, bɪˈkɔːz ɪt wʌz ɪˈliːɡəl, ʃiː ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "I was scared, but I loved the feeling of the spray can in my hand."
passage.reading: aɪ wʌz ˈskɛrd, bʌt aɪ ˈlʌvd ðə ˈfiːlɪŋ əv ðə ˈspreɪ ˌkæn ɪn maɪ ˈhænd.

passage.text: Five years ago, a café owner asked her to paint the wall outside his shop.
passage.reading: ˈfaɪv ˈjɪrz əˈɡoʊ, ə kæˈfeɪ ˈoʊnər ˈæskt hɜːr tə ˈpeɪnt ðə ˈwɔːl ˌaʊtˈsaɪd hɪz ˈʃɑːp.

passage.text: Her painting showed an old woman feeding cats in a narrow street, and it went viral.
passage.reading: hɜːr ˈpeɪntɪŋ ˈʃoʊd ən ˈoʊld ˈwʊmən ˈfiːdɪŋ ˈkæts ɪn ə ˈnæroʊ ˈstriːt, ənd ɪt ˈwɛnt ˈvaɪrəl.

passage.text: Since then, she has painted more than forty walls around the city.
passage.reading: sɪns ˈðɛn, ʃiː hæz ˈpeɪntɪd ˈmɔːr ðən ˈfɔːrti ˈwɔːlz əˈraʊnd ðə ˈsɪti.

passage.text: Now, hotels and companies pay her to paint their buildings.
passage.reading: ˈnaʊ, hoʊˈtɛlz ənd ˈkʌmpəniz ˈpeɪ hɜːr tə ˈpeɪnt ðɛr ˈbɪldɪŋz.

passage.text: Mook's work has received recognition in other countries, too.
passage.reading: ˈmuːks ˈwɜːrk hæz rɪˈsiːvd ˌrɛkəɡˈnɪʃən ɪn ˈʌðər ˈkʌntriz, ˈtuː.

passage.text: Last year, she was invited to paint a wall in Australia.
passage.reading: ˈlæst ˈjɪr, ʃiː wʌz ɪnˈvaɪtɪd tə ˈpeɪnt ə ˈwɔːl ɪn ɔːˈstreɪljə.

passage.text: "I'm happy that people see graffiti as art now," she says.
passage.reading: aɪm ˈhæpi ðæt ˈpiːpəl ˈsiː ɡrəˈfiːti əz ˈɑːrt ˈnaʊ, ʃiː ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "But my favorite walls are still the ones in my old neighborhood."
passage.reading: bʌt maɪ ˈfeɪvərɪt ˈwɔːlz ər ˈstɪl ðə ˈwʌnz ɪn maɪ ˈoʊld ˈneɪbərhʊd.

passage.text: "Art should be for everyone, not just for people who go to galleries."
passage.reading: ˈɑːrt ʃʊd bi fər ˈɛvriwʌn, ˈnɑːt dʒʌst fər ˈpiːpəl huː ˈɡoʊ tə ˈɡæləriz.
